newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Demirel says Turkey seeks EU membership soon.
newsitem.headline: Demirel says Turkey seeks EU membership soon.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel said on Thursday his country expected to join the European Union (EU) soon, and offered overseas manufacturers a base for wider access to the European market.

"We expect to be a full member of the EU in the near future. They (foreign investors) can invest in Turkey, produce and export to the European Union without tariff and non-tariff restrictions," he told leading Bangladeshi businessmen in Dhaka.
Turkey, which has an association agreement with the EU, was incensed this month when Christian Democrat leaders, including some heads of EU governments, declared it was unfit for membership.
But EU foreign ministers have distanced themselves from this view and assured Turkey it could one day qualify.

Demirel, who arrived Dhaka on Tuesday to attend Bangladesh's independence anniversary on Wednesday, told Bangladeshi businessmen that the Turkish economy was growing in strength following substantial reforms in the past decade.
He said 80 percent of Turkey's exports consisted of manufactured goods and its foreign trade turnover had reached $70 billion a year.

"Turkey is in a much better position to engage in the markets of Europe, the Middle East, Russia and Central Asia ...Now our businessmen are looking beyond its periphery and are ready to discover new markets in Asia, the Pacific Rim and Latin America."
Demirel, due to leave for home later on Thursday, brought more than 100 business executives who discussed business and investment opportunities with Bangladeshi entrepreneurs.
Demirel said Turkey was undertaking $4.5 billion worth of development projects in Central Asia and $6.1 billion in Russia.
He said Ankara was making progress in exploring for oil and natural gas in central Asia and transporting these resources through its territory.
"The pipeline projects we are proposing will elevate Turkey to a position of becoming the oil terminal of the region in the coming century," he said.
Demirel asked Bangladeshi businessmen to exploit the "experience of Turkey and its strategic location".
He suggested formation of a joint business council between the private sectors of the two countries.
Bangladesh is a member of a new Turkey-led economic bloc comprising eight Islamic countries, which is due to be formally launched in June at a summit in Ankara.

Yussuf Abdullah Harun, president of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Comemrce and Industry (FBCCI), said Bangladeshi entrepreneurs were keen for joint ventures with Turkey in fields like cement, leather products and engineering.
Trade between Dhaka and Ankara has been at a low level. In 1996, Bangladesh's exports to Turkey amounted to $17 million against its imports $3.5 million.
"It (trade) is minimal and should be increased," Demirel said.
